cadence_basis: Ten days is how often this app goes back and re-reads CDFW's results document. It is not a statement about how often CDFW publishes one; CDFW publishes no schedule.
season_label_basis: the season CDFW's own results heading on its waterfowl page names, never this app's calendar
current_season_heading_verbatim: 2026 / 2027 Waterfowl Hunt Results for State-operated Hunting Areas
expected_publication_basis: the page prints no publication date under its own current-season heading
columns_quote_exemption_reason: These are CDFW's own column headings, quoted. The two species columns name the species taken most and second-most in that cell on that hunt day; they are the department's names for its own columns, and this app publishes no ranking of places.
date_basis: day and month from the row, year from the season in the document's own title
year_rule: The document prints a month and a day and no year. A hunt date in July through December takes the season's first year; a hunt date in January through June takes the season's second year.
quarantine_rule: A page whose own printed title block names a different season is not read into this one. The rows on such a page carry a month and a day and no year, so reading them under this season's title would date every one of them a year wrong.
duplicate_rule: A page that prints the same title block and the same rows as an earlier page is a page the document repeats. Its rows are recorded once, under the first page that printed them, and the repeat is counted here.
join_rule: An area name is matched to a place in this app where the two published names are the same string, character for character, or where CDFW's own two spellings of one place are declared as a pair in curated/hunt_code_aliases_2026.json — its reservation form writes Gray Lodge WA and its land layer writes Gray Lodge Wildlife Area, and the owner declared on 2026-09-15 that this app may read those as one place. The only difference a declared pair may span is the words Wildlife Area, their abbreviation WA, or their absence; a name differing by any other word is a different place. Areas that match nothing are counted, never guessed.
join_normalisation_note: Eight of CDFW's ten Type A wildlife areas match: seven through a declared alias for the WA the reservation form abbreviates, and Imperial on its own spelling. North Grasslands and Upper Butte Basin match nothing and are counted, because form FG 1596 names their UNITS rather than the areas, and a unit's rule is not the area's.
alias_rule: A code or an area name is matched to a record in this app where the two published strings are the same string, character for character, OR where the pair is one of the spellings CDFW itself publishes for the same code or the same place and the owner has declared it in curated/hunt_code_aliases_2026.json, with both documents that carry it and their hashes. Nothing else is folded: no third spelling, no similarity, no nearest match. A string that matches nothing is counted, never guessed.
alias_limit_rule: An alias binds a spelling to a spelling. It publishes no value: every number, date and sentence beside a joined row is still the one its own source printed.
sentence_template: CDFW reported an average of {avg_waterfowl} waterfowl per hunter at {area} on {date}, {season}, across {hunters} hunters.
source_disclaimer: This is a count of a past hunt day. It is not a statement about any other day.
attribution: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
firewall: Every number in this file counts a bird or a hunter. It renders as a fact with its season and the date it was read, and it never moves a match count, a band or an ordering in this app.
pending_reason: CDFW heads its results page with this season and publishes no document behind that heading yet. This app has no rows for the season and says so; an empty table would read as a statement that nobody hunted.
